tasks.short: Check graduation requirements and write recommendations

steps.what: Review transcripts to ensure students meet graduation requirements.
Add the credit total in the workbook when no programme total exists.
Read the college entrance requirements in the handbook.
Judge whether the learner meets the graduation or college entrance requirements.
Write letters of recommendation from the transcripts and judgement.
Commit the graduation decision on the learner record.
Send the recommendation letter by e-mail to the college.
Tell the learner in person whether graduation requirements are met.

tasks.design: The {LMS} compares the learner transcript with required-module codes the programme administrator already keeps, and shows which required modules are still open. The career counselor reads those lines, including transfer and exemption lines the codes do not cover, judges graduation or college entrance, and writes the recommendation letter. The counselor commits the decision on the learner record and sends the letter by {EMAIL} only after accepting that letter. The talk with the learner stays in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Required modules sat in a handbook, and the credit total was added by hand, so each transcript was read line by line.
tasks.enabler_now: Module results are already on the {LMS}, so comparing them with required-module codes is configuration of that record.
tasks.still_hard: Transfer credits and exemptions are not in the module codes, and the letter still has to sound like this counselor.
tasks.human_edge: The counselor decides the borderline case and accepts the recommendation letter before it leaves.

ambition.what: Flag every learner whose required modules are still open, not only those who ask for a letter.

tasks.altitude: The counselor spends the week on borderline cases and letters, and can see every learner whose required modules are still open.

reach.task: Separate a requirement check from the recommendation that follows it.
reach.learn: Keep the letter tied to the transcript lines the counselor actually read.

evidence.claim: A learning record can show required modules still open when a programme administrator has already stored those module codes, and the counselor still decides the borderline case. Model knowledge.
Education records stay inside the organisation, and a recommendation letter leaves only after the counselor accepts that letter. Model knowledge.

assumptions: This design adds no monitoring or recording tool, so staff consent for one is out of scope.
The comparison only shows open required modules. The career counselor decides. It is not a solely automated decision.
Required-module codes are kept by the programme administrator. That upkeep is the other-role increment.
Focal upkeep is zero because the remaining transcript read sits in g1, acceptance of the decision sits in g6, and acceptance of the letter sits in g7.
Time shares follow this task's own means split: 19 on the learning record, 6 on the workbook, 7 on e-mail, 40 on documents, 28 in person.
No new credit-total record is written. The counselor stops adding one when module results already on the {LMS} carry the total.
unknowns: Whether this learning system already stores required modules as fields a comparison can read.
Which college addresses are already on the learner record.
research_questions: Does this learning system store required modules as fields the comparison can read?
Who may see the open-module list: the counselor only, or also the programme administrator?

already_counted.description: The career counselor accepts the graduation decision while committing it on the learner record.
The career counselor accepts the recommendation letter while sending it.

incremental.description: The programme administrator keeps required-module codes on the {LMS} so the comparison has codes to read.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is the case where the programme stores no required-module codes, so the counselor still reads every transcript line and still adds the credit total in the workbook. High is the case where those codes are present, the workbook total stops, and the letter, the commit, the send, and the talk stay at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Encourage learners to take on harder study

steps.what: Read untried courses that prepare students for later educational experiences.
Note finished courses in the workbook when completion is unmarked.
Read the learner goal notes before the conversation.
Encouraging students to explore learning opportunities and persevere with challenging tasks.
Write the session note after the conversation.
Commit the session note on the learner record.
Send the agreed next course by e-mail to the learner.

tasks.design: The {LMS} lists courses the learner has not tried, using completion flags the programme administrator already keeps. The career counselor still reads that short list and the learner's goal notes, then holds the encouragement conversation in person. Afterwards the counselor writes a session note, commits it on the learner record, and sends the agreed next course by {EMAIL} only after accepting that message.
tasks.previous_blocker: Untried courses were assembled by hand because finished courses were marked in a workbook rather than on the enrolment.
tasks.enabler_now: Completion flags on the {LMS} already say which courses are finished.
tasks.still_hard: Encouraging a learner to persevere is the conversation itself, and a course list does not do it.
tasks.human_edge: The counselor chooses what to push, and how hard, while the learner is in the room.
tasks.altitude: The week is still the encouragement conversations. Looking up untried courses is shorter.

reach.task: Keep the encouragement in the room with the learner.
reach.learn: A course list does not replace the conversation about sticking with a hard task.

evidence.claim: A learning record can list courses a learner has not tried when completion flags are already stored. The encouragement conversation stays with the counselor. Model knowledge.
A message to a learner naming an agreed next course leaves only after the counselor accepts that message. Model knowledge.

assumptions: This design adds no monitoring or recording tool, so staff consent for one is out of scope.
Completion flags are kept by the programme administrator. That upkeep is the other-role increment.
Focal upkeep is zero because the remaining course read sits in e1, acceptance of the session note sits in e6, and acceptance of the course message sits in e7.
Time shares follow this task's own means split: 6 on the learning record, 1 on the workbook, 10 on e-mail, 18 on documents, 65 in person.
The encouragement conversation is not shortened.
unknowns: Whether every course on this programme already has a completion flag.
research_questions: Which courses carry a completion flag on the learning record today?

already_counted.description: The career counselor accepts the session note while committing it.
The career counselor accepts the agreed-course message while sending it.

incremental.description: The programme administrator keeps course completion flags on the {LMS}.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is the case where the learning system has no completion flags, so the counselor still lists untried courses by hand and still notes finished courses in the workbook. High is the case where the flags exist, the workbook note stops, and the encouragement talk, the session note, the commit, and the e-mail stay at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Request professional sources by e-mail before the reading.
Open tests and scores on the assessment screen.
Find earlier records on the learner timeline.
Add subscale totals in the workbook when the screen shows none.
Hold interviews with students and individuals on personality characteristics.
Read the records, the tests, and the professional report.
Evaluate abilities, interests, and personality using tests, records, and sources.
Write the evaluation the counselor will commit.
Commit the evaluation on the learner record.

tasks.design: The career counselor requests professional sources by {EMAIL} before reading them. Scores open on the assessment screen, where the assessment officer has already stored them, and earlier enrolments open on the {LMS} timeline. Interviews stay in person. The counselor then evaluates abilities, interests, and personality, writes the evaluation, and commits it on the learner record. The evaluation is not sent outside.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scores, earlier records, and outside reports sat apart, and subscale totals were added in a workbook.
tasks.enabler_now: The assessment screen already stores the scores, and the {LMS} timeline already stores earlier enrolments.
tasks.still_hard: An interview, and a judgement about personality, cannot be reduced to the score on the screen.
tasks.human_edge: The counselor decides what the scores and the interview mean for this person.
tasks.altitude: The week is still the interviews and the evaluation. Opening stored scores and earlier records is shorter.

reach.task: Do not treat a test score as the evaluation.
reach.learn: The interview and the counselor's reading stay inside the decision.

evidence.claim: An assessment screen can show scores an assessment officer has already stored, and the counselor still reads them before evaluating. Model knowledge.
Ability and personality material stays on the learner record. This design does not send the evaluation outside the organisation. Model knowledge.

assumptions: This design adds no monitoring or recording of interviews, so staff consent for a recording tool is out of scope.
Test scores are stored by the assessment officer before the counselor opens the assessment screen. That upkeep is the other-role increment.
Focal upkeep is zero because reading scores sits in v2, reading the timeline sits in v3, accepting the source request sits in v1, and accepting the evaluation sits in v9.
Time shares follow this task's own means split: 9 on the assessment screen, 3 on the workbook, 6 on e-mail, 29 on documents, 53 in person.
The evaluation is committed on the learner record and is not sent outside.
unknowns: Whether these personality tests are treated as special-category data in this organisation.
Whether the assessment screen already shows subscale totals for every test in use.
research_questions: Are the personality tests used here treated as special-category data?
Which scores does the assessment officer store before the counselor opens the screen?

already_counted.description: The career counselor accepts the professional-source request while sending it.
The career counselor accepts the evaluation while committing it on the learner record.

incremental.description: The assessment officer stores test scores on the assessment screen before the counselor opens them.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is the case where the assessment screen stores no scores and the learner timeline has no earlier enrolments, so the counselor still gathers both and still adds subscale totals in the workbook. High is the case where both are already stored, the workbook totals stop, and the request, the interviews, the reading, the evaluation, and the commit stay at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Search provider pages for financial aid opportunities and trade schools.
Note aid deadlines in the workbook from the provider page.
Read technical topics on the published fact pages before choosing.
Choose degree programs against admission requirements for this learner.
Provide students information on college degree programs and apprenticeship programs.
Approve the programme list that will be sent.
Send the programme list by e-mail to the learner.

tasks.design: The career counselor searches provider pages for degree, aid, trade, technical, and apprenticeship facts, and checks that each quoted line means what that page says. A guidance information officer keeps the catalogue those pages are drawn from. The counselor chooses a fit, explains it to the learner in person, accepts the list the talk settled, and sends that same list by {EMAIL}. The send does not rewrite the accepted list.
tasks.previous_blocker: Facts were copied off provider pages into a workbook because the pages and the learner meeting were not connected.
tasks.enabler_now: The provider pages are public, and a maintained catalogue can hold a quote next to the page it came from.
tasks.still_hard: The learner's reaction in the room changes which facts are worth sending.
tasks.human_edge: The counselor decides which programme fits after hearing the learner, and accepts the list before it is sent.
tasks.altitude: The week is still the explanation in the room. Searching pages is shorter, and the e-mail leaves only after the talk.

reach.task: Quote the provider page rather than retell it from memory.
reach.learn: The learner hears the page, then the counselor's judgement of fit.

evidence.claim: A counselor can quote a public provider page and check that the quote means what the page says, then e-mail the list only after accepting the version settled in the talk. Model knowledge.
Programme facts may be public, and the list still leaves the organisation only after the counselor accepts the version that will be sent. Model knowledge.

assumptions: This design adds no monitoring or recording tool, so staff consent for one is out of scope.
The programme catalogue is kept by the guidance information officer. That upkeep is the other-role increment.
Focal upkeep is zero because the quote checks sit in p1 and p3, and acceptance of the post-talk list sits in p5.
Time shares follow this task's own means split: 6 on provider pages, 2 on the workbook, 11 on e-mail, 25 on documents, 56 in person.
p7 sends the list p5 accepted and does not rewrite it.
unknowns: Which provider pages the guidance information officer is already allowed to quote into the catalogue.
research_questions: Which provider pages are already in the catalogue the counselor is allowed to quote?

already_counted.description: The career counselor's review of the post-talk programme list is the acceptance of the version that will be sent.

incremental.description: The guidance information officer keeps the programme catalogue that the provider-page search quotes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is the case where provider pages cannot be quoted, so the counselor still reads each page in full and still notes aid deadlines in the workbook. High is the case where the pages are quoted, the workbook note stops, and the choice, the talk, the acceptance, and the e-mail stay at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The counselor still decides borderline entrance cases, still writes each recommendation, still runs the encouragement talk, and still interprets tests. The learning record only shortens looking up open modules and untried courses.
reach: From Health Education Specialists: turn a public programme fact into a short explanation a learner can repeat.
From Rehabilitation Counselors: separate a test score from the decision it supports.
From Social and Human Service Assistants: keep a referral request to the fact that source holds.
skills_to_grow: Check a quoted programme line against the page it came from.
Write a recommendation that uses only the transcript and the interview.
Say when a test score is not enough.
role.ambitious_version: Each week the counselor sees every learner whose required modules are still open and invites the ones who are close, instead of waiting for a letter request.

job.title: Educational, Guidance, and Career Counselors and Advisors
